title: Tests that pin incidental read interactions
pattern: A test verifies read-only collaborator calls (getters, database queries, data reads) as implementation steps, asserting *how* the system arrived at a result instead of the observable behavior those reads support.
why_bad: Non-state-changing interactions are private data-flow details. Harmless changes such as adding a cache lookup or reordering queries break the test without exposing a consumer-visible regression, while the actual result may remain unchecked [209, 518, 529].
detection: Mock or spy expectations (`verify()`, `times()`, ordering constraints) require specific getter, query, or read-only collaborator calls when those interactions are not themselves a documented behavioral requirement [530].
fix: Assert returned values and observable state instead of verifying reads [208, 526]. Keep interaction checks only where the interaction itself is part of the requirement (a state-changing operation), rather than an incidental way to calculate the result [518, 529].
source: *   *Software Engineering at Google*, "Interaction Testing" (p. 275-279) [208, 209, 525, 527, 529]; *   *Software Engineering at Google*, "Interaction Testing on Non-State-Changing Functions" (p. 275-276) [518, 529, 530]
